title: New Baby, Older Sibling: Easing the Transition
hook: A new baby is a big change for an older child. Prepare them ahead, expect some jealousy and regression, protect one-on-one time, skip comparisons, and coach them through the rough patches.
key_points: Prepare ahead: talk about the baby, read books together, and be honest that newborns cry and take a lot of time.
Expect some jealousy and regression (clinginess, thumb-sucking, potty accidents) — it's normal and usually temporary.
Protect daily one-on-one time so your older child knows your love hasn't shrunk.
Give them a real role in baby care, avoid comparing siblings, and coach them through conflict.
content_html: Welcoming a new baby reshapes an older child's whole world, so a little preparation goes a long way. The AAP suggests talking about the baby ahead of time, reading books about becoming a big sibling, and being honest — newborns are cute, but they also cry and soak up a lot of your attention. Timing big transitions like potty training before the baby arrives, rather than during the upheaval, can help too.
extra_html: After the baby comes, expect some jealousy and temporary regression — extra clinginess, thumb-sucking, or potty accidents are common and usually pass. The antidotes are reassurance and inclusion: carve out daily one-on-one time so your older child knows your love hasn't shrunk, and give them a genuine role in baby care, like fetching diapers or choosing an outfit. Avoid comparing siblings, and when squabbles come, coach them through it rather than always refereeing. This is general educational information from the AAP — if rivalry or distress feels persistent or intense, your pediatrician can offer guidance.

source.name: HealthyChildren.org (AAP) — Preparing Your Older Child for a New Baby

related.title: Positive Discipline: Teaching, Not Punishing
related.hook: Discipline means teaching, not hurting. The AAP's most effective tools are calm consistency, catching good behavior, and clear consequences — and it advises against spanking and harsh words.

related.title: Helping Kids Manage Big Feelings
related.hook: Young children can't yet calm themselves down on their own — they borrow your calm. Naming feelings and co-regulating now builds the self-regulation that grows with age.

flashcards.prompt: What's a normal reaction from an older child after a new baby arrives?

choices.text: Some jealousy and temporary regression, like clinginess or potty accidents
Permanent loss of skills they had learned
No reaction at all in a healthy child

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP notes older siblings commonly show jealousy and temporary regression after a new baby; it's normal and usually passes.

flashcards.prompt: Two ways to help an older child adjust to a new sibling?
flashcards.back_html: Protect one-on-one time so they feel loved, and give them a real role in baby care (bringing diapers, picking clothes). Prepare them ahead, avoid comparisons, and coach them through conflict.
